> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9004d45e412f42a2292bed32b3e8e1589521ae97` — the merge of head `9d8e0766babadc87e234df4c5073e63853ac5fc0` into base `2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9004d45e412f42a2292bed32b3e8e1589521ae97 && git checkout 9004d45e412f42a2292bed32b3e8e1589521ae97
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12 9d8e0766babadc87e234df4c5073e63853ac5fc0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12 && git merge --no-ff 9d8e0766babadc87e234df4c5073e63853ac5fc0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Scope: `.changeset/computed-field-follows-hidden-input.md`, `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/field-masker.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/formula-reads-hidden-field-masking.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-field-readers.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-inputs.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` + `packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts`, `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-security-resolvers.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`, `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` (cited code, read, not reviewed)

This record stays at the rule layer on purpose (field-level security, public repository). Where the rule is not kept it says so and grades it; the where and the how are in the seat's private notes, not here.

### ① Derived judgments

The rule the PR declares: a caller who cannot read a field, or is served it only partially masked, cannot read any computed field whose expression reads that field, directly or through another computed field, and that computed field is withheld exactly as the field it reads is.

What the tree keeps, read at this head:

- Result mask and query guard. The dependency closure is folded into the two field maps the plugin already masks and guards by, so `find`, `findOne`, the `insert` and `update` echo, the filter, sort and group positions, the aggregate input gate and the published query-side answer all inherit it from one derivation. Kept.
- Transitivity. The fold iterates to a fixed point over computed fields reading computed fields. Kept.
- Reads that cannot be named fail closed (hidden whenever any other field of the object is withheld from the caller). Kept, and declared.
- Union semantics. The fold runs after the most-permissive union across the caller's sets, after the per-field capability fold and after the delegator intersection, so a computed field is hidden only where the input is denied through every set the caller holds. A View All or Modify All holder and a system context are untouched. Kept.
- The read set. It is taken with the platform's one member reader, the one the engine plans formula evaluation by, so the fold and the engine cannot disagree about which spellings name a field. Kept.
- Caching. The read set is schema-derived and cached per object beside the masking rules; this change caches nothing per caller or per tenant. No bleed.
- Over-narrowing. Nothing a caller with full input access could read before is hidden now, beyond the two cases the changeset declares (unnameable reads; a partially masked input hides the computed field whole).

What the tree does not keep:

M1 (must-fix) — the rule is not kept on every reader. The PR's acceptance notes say that where a computed field stays listed, the caller's rows carry no value for it; read against the tree, that does not hold everywhere. Every reader that returns a computed value, or answers about one, must apply the same hide, each with its own pin and control. Seat's private notes, N-1 and N-2.

M2 (must-fix) — the rule is not kept on every input the declaration covers. The changeset and the docs sentence state the rule for any field a computed field's expression reads; the tree keeps less than that. Close it, or bring the declaration and the docs sentence down to what the tree keeps. Seat's private notes, N-3.

S1 (should-fix) — published contract sentences this head makes untrue and does not touch. `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` states the read projection is the exact complement of what the read path's field mask deletes, and that the query-side answer differs from it by exactly the fields the caller sees masked; the docblock of `getReadableFields` in `security-plugin.ts` and the comment in `computeReadableFields` (`security-plugin-field-readers.ts`), both files in this diff, state the same complement. After this head none of the three is true. Either the projection answers as the sentences say, or the sentences say what it now answers.

S2 (should-fix) — pins. The suite pins `find`, `findOne`, a projection, the `update` echo, the transitive case, the capability case, the masked-input case, filter and aggregate on a stored computed field, and five controls. Declared in the changeset or the PR body and unpinned: the `insert` echo; the sort and group positions; the published query-side answer (`getQueryableFields` no longer listing the field); a delegated caller; a caller holding two sets of which one grants the input (the union control); the fail-closed case end to end through the engine (it is pinned on the helper only). Each is one reader of the rule and wants its own pin with a control.

S3 (should-fix) — docs. The sentence added to `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx` states the rule and omits what an administrator will meet first: the fail-closed case for an expression whose reads cannot be named, the remedy (grant read on every input), and that the field stays listed. The changeset carries all three; the page is where they are looked for.

N1 (nit) — `computedFieldReads` is both the exported function in `field-masker.ts` and the posture field it fills; `security-plugin.ts` holds both names in one scope. It also parses each expression twice (once inside the member reader, once for the opacity walk); once per object, cached, so cost is not the point.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`, with the `!` title, the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset body. Correct by AGENTS.md step 3: nothing a metadata author can write is added, removed or re-meant, so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch`; a non-protocol breaking change keeps its banner and its ADR-0087 disposition at `patch`. The changeset carries exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), which fits: no key, value or stored row moves. Who moves, the before and after per reader, and the one-line remedy are all present. No objection to the level or the carrier. The declaration's SCOPE is what M2 and S1 are about, not its level.

CI at this head: 53 check-runs, all completed; 38 success, 15 skipped, none failing, none in progress. The verdict below does not wait on CI.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Published contract: `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` is not in the diff and two of its sentences about the field projections stop being true at this head (S1). The PR states "No change to `packages/spec`"; the behaviour it describes changed underneath it.
- The contract text that describes the field projections was not moved with this head (S1).
- No `packages/spec` schema, no governed path, no generated artifact is touched; `Skills-docs: none` is right as argued (a formula over a masked roll-up is withheld with it).
- `plugin-security` already depends on `@objectstack/formula`; the two new value imports add no package edge.
- Release-owned docs untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: it takes no declared capability away from a consumer who holds its inputs, and it makes field-level security's own refusal real for values computed from a refused field. The direction is right, the mechanism is the right one (one derivation folded into the maps the gates already read, the platform's one member reader, fail-closed where reads cannot be named), and the union, delegation, masking and bypass semantics are each handled where the existing folds handle them. Per file:

- `field-masker.ts`: the read set and the fixed-point fold agree with the engine's own planner where they apply; the opacity test errs toward hiding. Holds for what it covers; M2 is about what it does not.
- `security-plugin-object-inputs.ts`: both call sites are placed after every other fold and the masked-field handling is correct (a withheld computed field drops its own masking rule rather than being served masked). Holds.
- `security-plugin.ts`, `security-plugin-field-readers.ts`: the posture field is collected on both field-map shapes and carried by the zero-set stand-in. Holds. The docblocks in the same two files still promise what S1 names.
- test file: real engine, real driver, real plugin; rule tests and controls are separated and the controls are the right ones. Short of a pin per reader (S2).
- changeset and docs: the declaration is well-formed and honest about the two over-narrowing cases; it claims more than the tree keeps (M2), and one acceptance note does not hold on every reader (M1).

A security narrowing whose declared rule is not kept on every reader and every input path cannot pass on the readers it does cover: operators will read the changeset as the whole rule. Two must-fix.

### ① Derived judgments

The rule the PR declares at this head: a caller who cannot read a field, or is served it only partially masked, cannot read any computed field whose expression reads that field, on its own record, through another computed field, or on the record it reads through a reference; the computed field is withheld exactly as the field it reads is.

Prior findings, by id, against the tree at this head:

- Prior M1 (the rule is not kept on every reader): changed. The readers that serve a value now take the one fold. The part of M1 that made it a must-fix is closed. One part is not, and continues below as S1.
- Prior M2 (the rule is not kept on every input the declaration covers): changed, still open. The fix added the reference input, and the declaration grew with it; the declaration as now written is again wider than what the tree keeps. Continues below as M1.

- Prior S2 (pins): mostly closed. The `insert` echo, the sort and group positions, the query projection, a delegated caller, the union control and the fail-closed case through the engine are each pinned now. What remains continues below as S2.

Re-walked at this head and kept: transitivity (fixed point); union semantics (the fold runs after the most-permissive union, the capability fold and the delegator intersection); fail closed where reads cannot be named and where the referenced object's answer cannot be had; no per-caller or per-tenant state cached by this change; a system context and a View All or Modify All holder untouched.

This head withholds only over a declared field the caller may not read there, and loses nothing the rule held for such a field. Nothing was found that a caller with full input access could read before and cannot now, beyond what is declared, with one undeclared case (S3).

What the tree does not keep:

M1 (must-fix) — continues prior M2. The rule is not kept on every input the declaration covers. The changeset, the docs sentence and the PR body each state the rule for inputs the tree does not withhold over. Close it, or bring all three down to what the tree keeps. Seat's private notes, N-5 and N-6.

S1 (should-fix) — continues prior M1, regraded. The rule is not kept on every reader. The grade, and why it is no longer a must-fix, are in the seat's private notes, N-2.

S2 (should-fix) — continues prior S2. Pins. `bb0d74cb` changed the rule of the reference-read arm and changed no test: the narrowed case has neither a pin nor a control, and the PR body's ablation of that arm stands on the three tests written for the rule before it was narrowed. The reference input is not pinned at every reader that reads it. The delegated pin calls the masker directly rather than driving a delegated read through the engine. Whatever closes M1 and S1 wants its own pin with a control.

S3 (should-fix) — new. The public-form echo now withholds every computed field that reads through a reference, for every submitter. The PR body says so; the changeset's account of who moves does not, and nothing pins it. It is a fail-closed narrowing and belongs in the declaration operators read.

N1 (nit) — new. The docs sentence for the fail-closed case reads "whenever the caller may not read any other field of the object", which can be read as "no other field"; the changeset says "some other field", which is what the code does.

N2 (nit) — new. `b91c8739` moved the docs remedy from a role to a permission set; the changeset's "who moves" and remedy paragraphs still speak of a role being granted read.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`, with the `!` title, the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset body, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). Still correct by AGENTS.md step 3 after the delta: nothing a metadata author can write is added, removed or re-meant; no key, value or stored row moves; the breaking change is a runtime narrowing carried at `patch` with its banner. No objection to the level or the carrier. The declaration's scope is what M1 and S3 are about, not its level.

CI at this head: 72 check-runs, all completed; 60 success, 12 skipped, none failing, none in progress. The verdict below does not wait on CI.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Published contract: `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` is untouched and its sentences about the field projections are true at this head. "No change to `packages/spec`" now holds in substance as well as in the diff.
- `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` gains one ledger row classifying the new caller of the reference-target arbiter as not a served read. Read against the code, the classification is right: it names the referenced object to ask the caller's own projection there and reads no record of it.
- The two `describe_object` pins (`packages/runtime`, `packages/mcp`) moved by rule, with a control each, not loosened.
- The security plugin now asks, per operation on an object with a computed field reading through a reference, the caller's projection of each referenced object. It is asked once per operation and only by the readers that need it; no new package edge.
- No `packages/spec` schema, no governed path, no generated artifact, no release-owned docs touched. `Skills-docs: none` stands as argued.

### ④ Design judgment

The direction and the mechanism are right, and better than at the previous head: one derivation, one parse, folded into the map every reader already reads, with the projection made to answer as the mask does rather than the contract text being rewritten to excuse it. The narrowing takes nothing from a consumer who holds its inputs. Per file:

- `field-masker.ts`: the reader accounts for every use of the record root and errs toward hiding; the fold is a clean fixed point. M1 applies here.
- `security-plugin-object-inputs.ts`: the three fold sites sit after every other fold; a withheld computed field drops its own masking rule. After `bb0d74cb` it no longer over-narrows. M1 applies here.

- changeset and docs: well-formed and now complete on the fail-closed case and the remedy; they claim more inputs than the tree keeps (M1) and omit one narrowing (S3).

Five of six prior findings are closed or reduced, and the remaining distance is small. But a security narrowing is read by operators as the whole rule: while the declaration names inputs the tree does not withhold over, it cannot pass. One must-fix.
